steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook bow tie pasta at a boil, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain.

Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Whisk in flour, salt, and pepper; cook and stir until smooth and fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes. Whisk in milk, a little at a time, then bring to a boil and cook for 1 minute. Stir Colby cheese and mustard; cook, stirring occasionally, until cheese is melted. Remove from the heat and stir in pasta and ham. Pour mixture into a 2-quart baking dish and sprinkle Parmesan over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly and golden, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ham and Cheese Bow Ties
raw_recipe.description: Bow tie mac and cheese with strips of ham baked in a Colby cheese sauce and topped with Parmesan.

video.description: The way to make mac & cheese better than ever is to make it homemade, and your entire family will love the surprise of switching out macaroni for fun bowtie pasta! After cooking your pasta, cook garlic in butter, then whisk in flour, salt and pepper. Slowly stir in milk to create a white sauce. Mix in mustard and Colby cheese and stir until melted. Add the pasta along with ham and pour everything into a baking dish with a topping of Parmesan cheese. Bake until bubbly and serve to a very happy family or special guests.

review.reviewBody: Ok, I did this a lot differently. First of all, you should probably add more pasta if you don't want too much of the sauce. I omitted the mustard. I added 1 cup colby and 1/1/2 cup mozzarella and then salt, pepper and italian seasonings. Oh ya, and peas. Was a great dish, will definately make again. This is a good recipe to keep around just for the fact that you can do so much with it(use it as a base). Maybe add chicken or turkey and/or french cut green beans next time. Maybe top it off with some sliced cherry tomatoes.

WOW is all i can say!! I did as the other comments said and used less milk and cheese so it wouldn't be too saucy. I put a 1 1/4 cups of milk, 2 cups of cheese, and a little less of a 1/4 cup of flour and i used whole wheat flour. I didn't have colby so i used cheddar which turned out awesome anyway. I added dill weed and used Dijon like some of the comments suggested. After i boiled the pasta i let it cool and i cooked some carrots, broccoli, and, celery separately and added it to the pasta and ham before i added the sauce. Then after i added the sauce i added fresh spinach. Like i said before i used cheddar instead of Colby and topped it with freshly grated mozzarella instead since i didn't have any Parmesan. It came out BEAUTIFUL first of all.. Second it tasted very good. I was glad i added the veggies though because it is pretty rich from the cheese. Next time i'll add more seasoning though. 1/8 ts of pepper wasn't enough spice for me. The last thing i did differently was i LIGHTLY sprayed the bottom of the dish with Pam cooking spray and when i took it out it came out of the pan CLEAN. I'm thinking of adding green onion as a topper along with the cheese next time too. Overall very good! I don't like ham much and my SO doesn't either BUT we loved it in this dish.

Very good! I'll use this method of making a roux, adding the milk and then stirring in the cheese to make the sauce from now on for Mac & Cheese. I found the ratio of ingredients perfect. I didn't have Colby so I used a shredded cheese blend of mild cheddar and jack. Still mild. I will try all white cheddar next time. We like a little zing so I added 1 cup of finely diced sweet onion & 2 tsp cayenne pepper. Used Dijon instead of dry.
Added more pasta, ham and a can of small peas. Left out the parm and didn't bake. Not bad for Easter ham leftovers.
It was pretty good! Definitely different. I used another user's advice and used 1 cup Monterey, 1 cup sharp cheddar, and 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese. Also used Dijon mustard.

I have made this recipe many times, sometimes exactly following the recipe and other times changing it. I have added an extra 1/2 cup of milk and I have also made it with four different cheeses using the required amount. I have used soft cheese like havarti . I also made this with cut up roasted chicken and it was delicious.

Pretty good! I used 1lb of pasta and doubled the sauce, it was the perfect amount! The cheese sauce as written is extremely bland, but I added some cayenne, seasoned salt, another clove of garlic and some diced onion, it helped. It was a great way to use up leftover Easter ham. Served with a green salad for a full meal.

Very good, but I had to make a couple of substitutions. I had no bowties so used Rotini instead. Also didn't have Colby so used 1/2 mozzerella and 1/2 white cheddar. Put 1/2 cup of leftover peas and carrots in to use them up. Will make again for sure!
Winner! This is one of our favourites. I use Mexican cheese and velveeta. Add peas, one dish meal. Applesauce makes a good side.

I tweaked the recipe and chose a cheddar, american and swiss cheese mixture instead of the colby cheese, used dijon mustard instead of regular mustard and added panko italian bread crumbs over the top before baking...it was delicious! Will definitely be making again!!
I followed the recipes except I added a little nutmeg in the mix. For color, I added some dried chives & parsley. And a sprinkle of paprika on top.
I think the mustard ruined the cheese sauce. There was too much sauce.

Perfect as is. I did add frozen peas as we just happen to love them. Previous reviews said it freezes well also - love to know that! Would be a g7reat food gift for a friend or great potluck dish. Reheats well. Try with dijon....

Very good!! Used 1/2 colby and the rest a mix of stronger cheeses. Cheddar, italian mix and more parmesan. I increased ingredients.. some I doubled (pasta and the meat), and some I just increased 1 1/2 times. Used very little salt. Doubling the pasta made it just enough to fill a 13x9 pan! After I added the parmesan on top I sprinkled on some panko bread crumbs for some crunchiness. It was AWESOME. My mom loved it and my I-hate-pasta son even liked it!
Fairly easy to make. Great taste. So much better than the boxed mac and cheese. Will make it again.
I added chopped broccoli for some added greens and it was awesome.

"Make it anytime you want to," says it all. So simple he can learn to make it anytime he wants to and it will be just as tasty.

It's mac and cheese wearing a bow-tie.
Used Colby Jack. Everyone loved it. A keeper.
My family loved this recipes - even ate the leftovers!
This was good. Tasted like mac and cheese with ham added. Nothing special but a good quick family meal. Followed recipe and not sure if I would make again.
